messages:
sec-scan-bot: automated scanner flagged a public gist containing what looks like a live service token: gist.github.com/0a1b2c3d - file: infra/ingest.tf -> contains service_token = "sk_live_4fa7...". detected 2026-02-25 14:02 UTC

alex: taking point. I'm going to revoke that token immediately and provision a replacement. @sec-oncall please start impact analysis (logs, usage, customer access).

sec-oncall: received. query: searching auth logs for token pattern sk_live_4fa7* and associated requests. will also check KMS audit and any IAM role mappings.

kevin: FYI looks like the token is a long-lived service token used by internal ingest workers (env var INGEST_SERVICE_KEY). I see the gist references our repo name, likely a dev accidentally pasted tf var.

alex: revoking now. command: `curl -X POST https://internal.api/keys/revoke -d '{"key":"sk_live_4fa7xxxxxxxx"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'`

deploy-bot: revoke request accepted for key id key-0a9f, status: revoked.

sec-oncall: revoke confirmed. provisioning new key key-1b2c and rotating envs. Pushing deploys to staging and prod for ingest service. Will rotate any CI secrets referencing old key.

maria: did the leaked token access any customer orgs or S3 buckets with customer data? cs/alerts want to know if we need customer notification.

kevin: log summary: 173 requests using that token between 2026-02-24 22:14 and 2026-02-25 01:58 UTC. All requests hit the ingest endpoint /v1/ingest and internal caching; none matched endpoints tagged customer-data-read or /v1/user/* in our routing. No S3 access logs with that token.

lina: KMS audit: no key wrapping/unwrapping events tied to that token. The token had only ingest pipeline RBAC scope (write to internal cache). Good sign.

sec-oncall: escalation decision: classify as low-customer-impact but medium-internal-risk. Actions: 1) rotated token (done), 2) scan for other occurrences of same token and rotate if found, 3) disable public gist creation for corp org and block gists referencing our repo name, 4) add pre-commit hook + repo secret scanning, 5) create compliance ticket to wrap service tokens with KMS (short TTL + automatic rotation).

alex: opened SEC-1427 with remediation tasks and owners. Also flagged to infra to add short TTLs and constrained service identities.

maria: preparing internal comms for CS/legal: brief summary + confirmation no customer data accessed, actions taken, and monitoring window for any delayed access. Will wait for final logs export.

kevin: exporting full request logs and saving to /var/log/security/incidents/1795502468.log and uploading a hashed snapshot to the incident binder.

sec-oncall: closing operational containment. Postmortem items: root cause = developer pasted terraform snippet with hardcoded var to public gist; detection = automated public-gist scanner; gap = we don't yet enforce org-level disallow for public gists and many service tokens are long-lived. Remediation owner list in SEC-1427.

alex: thanks everyone. next steps: follow SEC-1427, verify rotation for any tokens matching same policy, add RBAC rule tightening, and schedule a short training reminder about secret handling. :thumbsup:

maria: noted — will coordinate CS comms and watch for any customer escalations.

sec-oncall: will run 72h extended monitoring and report back here with any anomalous calls.

alex: closing thread once 72h monitoring window completes.
